title: run_post_pipeline ignores extract_injection_source return value
description: In lifecycle.rs run_post_pipeline (lines 812-814): extract_injection_source is called and returns an InjectionSource, but the very next line hardcodes injection_source = InjectionSource::NntpPost. The comment even explains why: 'trusting the header would allow forgery'. But that means the whole extract_injection_source call is dead code — it extracts and returns the value and the value is thrown away. The header IS removed from article_bytes (that side-effect matters), but the returned enum is silently discarded. If the design intent is that injection_source is always NntpPost via NNTP POST, the call to extract_injection_source should just not return a value (or should not exist at all). As-is, a future developer will assume the returned value is used and may be confused. Actual correctness impact: the injection_source passed to append_to_groups is always NntpPost, which may suppress peering for SmtpListId articles that came in via the SMTP drain.
